items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: He'd bring his corner out there and take a pair of sticks and cymbals and so forth. And Eastwood would take his banjo and we'd have a jam session.

ctx.x: Well, on our intermission, at least around noon, we'd go get our lunch and we'd go out to the street. He'd bring his corner out there and take a pair of sticks and cymbals and so forth. And Eastwood would take his banjo and we'd have a jam session. Mm-hmm. And we had a wonderful time together on our intermission on 12 o'clock lunch. And then later on, I played a couple of jobs with the band, see. And he had Brownlee playing piano and Emmett Hardy playing cornet and so forth. And then later on, later on I played…
Yeah, it's still there. It's exterminated.

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: I mean, we, we, we used to play with, with Bill, uh, Eastwood. Bill Eastwood on banjo. Yeah. And we, we played that, and he played, played the Panama

ctx.x: Did he ever play Panama? Did you ever hear him play Panama? Yeah.

I mean, we, we, we used to play with, with Bill, uh, Eastwood. Bill Eastwood on banjo. Yeah. And we, we played that, and he played, played the Panama and he'd get, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, dun, dun, dun, dun, dun, you know, like, like, like, like I put that last, last chorus of Rampart Street bass.
